{"id": "117cebcc-f59a-44a7-a8e7-2a0b20e8fb6a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Application vs Network Load Balancer Differences Explained"}]}

{"id": "b46936f0-bc42-4a3d-bd27-3b9195a2c53d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "# ALB vs. NLB

The main difference is the layer each one works at. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) routes at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS). A Network Load Balancer (NLB) routes at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS).

| | **ALB** | **NLB** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TLS, TCP_UDP |
| **Routing** | Content-based: host, path, headers, query strings, HTTP method, source IP | Port and protocol only |
| **Performance** | Good for web traffic, with slightly higher latency | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency, and it handles sudden spikes well |
| **IP addressing** | Dynamic IPs, so you use its DNS name | One static IP per AZ, and you can attach your own Elastic IPs |
| **Client source IP** | Passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | Preserved natively, depending on target type |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023), but optional |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS, with SNI and authentication through Cognito or OIDC | Can terminate TLS or pass it through to the targets |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda, containers | Instances, IPs, ALB (as a target) |
| **Extra features** | Redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, WAF integration | PrivateLink (VPC endpoint services), static IPs for allow-listing |

## When to use which

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You run web apps, REST APIs, or microservices that need path-based or host-based routing, for example `/api` to one service and `/app` to another.
- You want WAF, user authentication, redirects, or Lambda targets.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need extreme performance, with millions of requests per second and very low latency.
- You have non-HTTP protocols such as gaming, IoT, VoIP, or custom TCP/UDP services.
- You need static or Elastic IPs, for example so partners can allow-list your addresses.
- You want to expose a service privately through AWS PrivateLink.

You can also combine them. Putting an NLB in front of an ALB gives you static IPs and PrivateLink support plus Layer 7 routing.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
